_meta.simulation_note: Simulated state advanced to 2026-08-10 (Sprint 20 Day 1). Sprint 17 closed Jul 10 (324/335 pts), Sprint 18 closed Jul 24 (341/350), Sprint 19 closed Aug 7 (352/360 — highest velocity of the year). Sprint 20 opened Aug 10. Key closures in the window: NEXUS M6 IAM Jul 1, NEXUS M5 CI/CD Jul 3, SHIELD M4 100 controls Jul 15, HORIZON M6 beta Jul 22, HORIZON M7 store submission Aug 1, SHIELD M5 evidence Aug 7 (reopened Jul 16 on Deloitte findings), PULSE M4 FlowEngine Aug 7. Missed: MERIDIAN M6 mid-market (Aug 1 → revised Aug 21, DR-015). Decisions DR-011 to DR-015 applied. Epic-level data reflects Aug 10 snapshot; milestone outcomes sourced from Aha! as SoT. Full event ledger: 1-inputs-triggers/simulation-log.json.

blockers.summary: 14 controls blocked on NEXUS IAM — RESOLVED Jul 1
blockers.status: RESOLVED — NEXUS IAM deployed Jun 30 22:05, M6 closed Jul 1. All 14 controls assigned Jul 1 morning and closed Jul 11–14. Blocker open 137 days.
blockers.note: DR-001 authorized May 1. Fatima's pre-staged assignments meant the team started the morning IAM went live — the 14 controls took 13 days from unblock to close.

epics.changeNote: COMPLETE Jul 15. Log retention (86th non-IAM) closed Jun 30. All 14 IAM-blocked controls closed Jul 11–14 following the Jul 1 unblock. 100/100 controls complete — M4 closed on time. Note: 3 of these controls (A1.7, CC6.4, CC6.6) subsequently failed Deloitte evidence review Jul 16 — control implementation was complete, evidence sufficiency was not. Tracked in SHIELD-4.

epics.summary: Vanta evidence collection and audit preparation

blockers.summary: Deloitte evidence sufficiency failure — 3 controls lack operating history
blockers.status: RESOLVED Aug 7. A1.7 (log retention, closed Jun 30), CC6.4 (quarterly access review certification) and CC6.6 (privileged access management) — the last two live only since Jul 1 — carried days of operating history where Type II requires months. Remediation Jul 20 – Aug 5: re-collected evidence with 30+ days where available, compensating documentation for the IAM pair. Deloitte confirmed sufficiency Aug 7.
blockers.note: This finding is what forced the certification-date question into the open. See DR-014 — the Aug 31 board mandate was restated as audit-readiness, with the Type II report at Dec 15.

epics.changeNote: Full 100-control package delivered to Deloitte Jul 15 on target. REOPENED Jul 16 on evidence sufficiency findings against 3 controls. Remediated and accepted Aug 7. Scope grew 80 → 110 SP for the remediation work.

epics.linkedMilestone: M6 — SOC 2 Type II audit readiness
epics.changeNote: NEW epic opened Jul 23 following DR-014. The Jul 16 finding showed that building a control and operating one are different problems. This epic covers monitoring, evidence automation, and drift detection across all 100 controls ahead of the Sep 1 observation window. Any control that drifts during Sep 1 – Nov 30 restarts its clock and moves the Dec 15 report.

epics.summary: DataCore pipeline migration — Airflow to Temporal (180 pipelines)

epics.summary: FlowEngine pipeline migration — Airflow to Temporal (340 pipelines)

blockers.summary: Stream Processing team capacity reallocation — resolved Jun 15 (DR-009)
blockers.status: RESOLVED and validated. Sprint 17 closed at 22 items against the ~20/sprint needed, confirming the DR-009 reallocation worked. DR-013 (Jul 10) chose to continue without descoping on that evidence.
blockers.note: The week-1 signal of 9 items that worried the Jul 6 escalation list was a ramp artifact, not a trend.

blockers.summary: Final 27 pipelines — undocumented cross-pipeline state dependencies
blockers.status: RESOLVED Aug 7. The last 27 FlowEngine pipelines shared state through side-channels the migration runbook never captured. Each needed manual dependency tracing before it could be cut over. Cost: 13 days and $180K of additional dual-run.
blockers.note: Root cause for the Jul 25 miss. Worth a retro line: the runbook (M2) was validated against DataCore, whose pipelines are far less entangled than FlowEngine's.

epics.changeNote: COMPLETE Aug 7. 340/340 migrated, 13 days late against the DR-009 revised target of Jul 25 — but still 5 days ahead of the original Aug 12 date. Trajectory: 200 (Jun 28) → 224 (Jul 5) → 252 (Jul 10) → 289 (Jul 24) → 313 (Jul 25) → 340 (Aug 7). Total dual-run cost at close: $1.38M against a $1.2M projection.

epics.summary: Airflow decommission — traffic verification, read-only mode, shutdown
epics.changeNote: NEW epic, started Aug 10 — nothing could begin until M4 closed. Now the critical path for the whole program. Dual-run cost stops only when Airflow is actually off, so every week here is $380K. Sequence: traffic verification (Aug), read-only mode (early Sep), shutdown (Sep 30). Seven weeks for work that has never been rehearsed on this estate.
